title: The mandatory secret-redaction and protection corpus
note: P13-T008's 'mandatory secret/protection fixtures'. Every entry is either a case this suite drives (kind: hook_ingest, check, full_recording_on_disk) or a pointer at the test that already drives it (kind: covered_by) -- and a pointer is checked to exist, so this list cannot decay into prose. Every entry's promised_by binds it to a sentence in docs/ (or in the code that asserts it); the suite fails if a sentence stops being there, so a withdrawn promise takes its fixture with it. What this corpus does NOT confirm is in not_confirmed, printed on every run. Run it with `cargo test -p sure-cli --test privacy_suite`.
license_note: Every secret in this file is invented and matches a detector's shape, not a real credential.

cases.title: A real `sure` run with no settings file of any kind stores the event and no recording
cases.why: This is acceptance line 1, named. The event must be observable afterwards -- a store that is empty because the hook failed would pass an assertion about an absence for the wrong reason -- so the case requires a stored event row beside the missing recording.

promised_by.says: Explicit opt-in may store:
Do not require durable storage of full prompt/response/terminal content.

cases.title: The decision path writes a decision row and still no recording
cases.why: The hook opens the store twice -- once for the event, once for the decision -- and the recording decision is taken once, before both. A default that only held on the event path would be a default with a hole in it, so the case requires both writes to have happened and no third row.

promised_by.says: Explicit opt-in may store:
The mode in effect is the stricter of the two settings files

cases.title: A project's own sure.yaml cannot carry a credential, and the value is not echoed when it tries
cases.why: The structural half of secret redaction: the value never has to be redacted because the file is refused before it is read into anything. The case also requires the store to be untouched, because a refusal that had already recorded something would be a refusal that leaked.

promised_by.says: Redaction must occur before user-visible reports and preferably before durable recording/model context.
avoid logging raw environment values;

cases.title: `protection.mode: custom` is refused by a check rather than accepted
cases.why: PROTECTION_MODE.md promises the setting is refused rather than accepted, and that a project believing it had rules SURE does not implement is the failure being avoided. Status 5 and an empty store are the observable form of 'stopped rather than accepted'.

promised_by.says: Not implemented in this release.
a settings file naming it is **refused** rather than accepted

files.README.md: # a project asking for protection rules this release does not have

cases.title: The same unimplementable setting is answered under strict when a harness meets it
cases.why: The other half of the refusal, and the one that must not fail open: a hook cannot stop and cannot ask, so a settings file it cannot read has to leave the user with more protection rather than less. The held read of a credential is how 'strict' is observed from a launcher.

promised_by.says: answers under `strict`, the firmest mode this release implements, and never under the default
a user who cannot be asked must not end up with less protection than they set.

cases.title: Failing firm is strict and not a blanket refusal
cases.why: Without this control, the case above would pass for a hook that refused everything, which is a different product -- and a hook that refused everything is a hook a user turns off, which leaves them with less protection than either case is about. The same project whose mode SURE cannot read lets an ordinary read through.

promised_by.says: `strict` differs from `standard` on the categories named above and on nothing else.

cases.title: A credential in `--goal` is in no byte of the store, and the redacted form is
cases.why: The report-and-storage seam for a value that arrives on the command line rather than from the project. Both halves are required: the absence proves nothing on its own, because a run that wrote no goal at all would satisfy it -- the redacted text being present is what shows SURE really did store the words it was given. The stdouts assertion requires the run to have said it recorded the goal, so the store half is about a goal that was recorded rather than about a setting that was never written. What the report prints is not asserted here; see not_confirmed[the-report-shows-a-goal-the-history-does-not-hold].

promised_by.says: Redaction must occur before user-visible reports and preferably before durable recording/model context.

cases.title: With recording turned on, the recording on disk still holds no secret
cases.why: The consent-times-redaction seam, at the only layer that can reach it: `persist_full_recording` redacts the payload before it is written, so opting in changes what is kept and not whether it is redacted. Every byte under the store directory is read, because the claim is about the file and not about the value a reader is handed back.
cases.layer_note: In-process, and it has to be: the consent comes from the user's own settings file, which on Windows is `%APPDATA%\SURE\sure.yaml` -- no flag, no environment variable and no test may redirect or write it (`Paths::discover_at` moves the store and not the settings). The writes are the same two calls `sure hook ingest` makes, through the same normalizer. See not_confirmed[no-recording-through-the-binary].

promised_by.says: redact stdout/stderr before persistent full-recording write where feasible;
full terminal output;

cases.title: What SURE decided about one request is a row the user can read and remove
cases.why: The audit trail end to end: a warn, a block and an allow that came from an allowance are written, readable through `sure history show`, and removed by the delete that removes their session. Not repeated here -- the corpus's hook cases read the rows back with the store API instead.

promised_by.says: `sure history show <SURE_SESSION_ID>` prints one session with the events in it, the record each event wrote, and the decision SURE reached about it where the event asked for one

cases.title: A store SURE cannot write leaves the answer the hooks reached intact and says the record is missing
cases.why: The failure direction of the audit trail: recording is best-effort and the verdict is not. It is a claim about a store that cannot be opened, which a process-level case would have to arrange by making a directory unreadable -- a per-platform trick this suite does not need, since the assertion is about what the hook returns rather than about what a launcher sees.

cases.title: Every run that reads settings says which mode was in effect and what it did about models
cases.why: The user-facing half of the privacy statement, asserted at the layer the user meets it. It is the promise in PRIVACY.md's last paragraph, and it is checked for a run that stopped as well as a run that finished.

promised_by.says: **The report states which mode was in effect and whether a model was consulted**, on every run that reads settings, including a run that stopped.

cases.title: The mode a run reports is the arbitrated one, and every state says what it means
cases.why: What the report's sentence is computed from. A statement built from the project's own file would be the report agreeing with the thing it is supposed to report about, and that is the failure these tests exist to make impossible.

cases.title: A project's own files cannot move the store, the mode a hook decides under, or a run's own answer
cases.why: P13-T009's rule, and the one the whole corpus rests on: a fixture project is a directory of files somebody else wrote, and a case is only about what SURE decides if none of those files can decide it. The corpus's own cases name their store on the command line for the same reason.

not_confirmed.what: `sure check --goal "..."` prints the goal verbatim under 'Your goal was written to the history as record N', and the history holds the redacted form. The sentence is about the record, so it describes a record that is not the one that was written.
not_confirmed.evidence: The case `a-secret-typed-into-a-goal-reaches-the-store-only-redacted` asserts the store half and passes: every byte under the store directory holds `deploy using token *** please` and no byte holds the credential. The report half is asserted by nothing, because the honest expectation is not settled. The two surfaces are `crates/sure-cli/src/check.rs` (`what_was_recorded`, the sentence and the verbatim text) and `crates/sure-core/src/store/mod.rs` (`redact_document`, applied to every document a write accepts).
not_confirmed.would_settle_it: A decision about which of the two rules wins for the goal: PROJECT_INTENT.md says the text is stored verbatim -- 'minus nothing' -- and the store redacts every document it accepts. Either the report prints what the store holds, or the goal is exempted from the store's redaction and the document says so. The corpus entry above should then become an assertion about the report as well as the store.

not_confirmed.what: No case here opens a full recording through the real `sure` process. The consent is read from the user's own settings file alone (`Authority::full_recording`), that file is not redirectable on Windows, and no test may write the machine's own settings.
not_confirmed.evidence: `a-full-recording-written-under-consent-is-redacted-on-disk` is `layer: store` for exactly this reason, and its expectations are about the file the store wrote rather than about what a process decided. `crates/sure-cli/tests/cli_contract.rs` says the same thing in `a_project_that_asks_for_full_recording_does_not_get_one`, whose retention number 'is not observable from here'.
not_confirmed.would_settle_it: A caller-named settings location -- a flag or a documented test hook that moves the user's settings the way `--store-dir` moves the store -- after which this case can be driven by a process and asserted at the binary layer like the others.

not_confirmed.what: `evaluation/acceptance-manifest.json` marks `dangerous-delete`, `force-push` and `sensitive-read` release-blocking, and the scenarios behind the three acts belong to P14-T008 rather than to this corpus. As this tree stands the three declarations exist and are graded: each of `fixtures/adversarial/dangerous-delete/`, `fixtures/adversarial/force-push/` and `fixtures/adversarial/sensitive-read/` holds a `scenario.json` with a `dangerous_action` block and a `README.md`, and `crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs` drives `hook_protection` over every declared run in-process, through the same `assess_claude_code_tool` / `assess_cursor_tool` the integrations call. This corpus covers the mode being the one in force and the decision about one request being recorded; it does not build those three scenarios, and they remain P14-T008's acceptance ('Delete/force-push/sensitive-read expected protection behavior tested'). This entry was written when `dangerous-delete` was a stub that carried `fixture_status: to_be_implemented_by_task_graph` and the other two had no directory: that was true then and stopped being true at P14-T008, and what the seam is about — who owns the three scenarios, and that this corpus does not grade them — did not move with it.
not_confirmed.evidence: `fixtures/adversarial/dangerous-delete/`, `fixtures/adversarial/force-push/` and `fixtures/adversarial/sensitive-read/` each hold a `scenario.json` declaring its runs and a `README.md`, which is a measurement of this tree rather than an inference from a brief; the three ids are named in `DANGEROUS_ACTION_FIXTURES` in `crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs` and in `crates/sure-testkit/tests/fixture_apps.rs`. The rule the three acts are held by is covered here, in the entry `the-three-acts-an-allowance-reaches-are-holds-and-only-those`.
not_confirmed.would_settle_it: P14-T008's fixtures, which are written: the seam is closed in the direction it opened, and no case here is owed for it. What it records now is the ownership boundary rather than an open question — the three scenarios are graded by P14-T008's test file and not by this corpus, and a case here whose expectation depended on one of those three acts would be a second owner for the same acceptance. There is none.
